title: All agree: no grace is needed to keep some precepts as to substance with a vicious motive
source_text: VIII. Nullus quoque eorum negat gratia opus non esse, ut quaedam legis praecepta quoad operis substantiam serventur: sed ita tamen ut actio moraliter bona & honesta non sit, ut quae ex malo fine, & cupiditate prava vitietur. Quod per se notum & manifestum est.
pass_a_gloss: VIII. None of them also denies that there is no need of grace that certain precepts of the law be kept as to the substance of the work: but yet so that the action be not morally good and honest, as being vitiated by an evil end and depraved desire. Which is known and manifest of itself.
pass_b_english: None of them denies, either, that some precepts can be kept as to the substance of the work without grace, but only so that the act is not morally good and honourable, being spoiled by a bad end and corrupt desire. That is obvious in itself.

lemmas.gloss: that there is no need of grace

lemmas.latin: ex malo fine, & cupiditate prava vitietur
lemmas.gloss: be vitiated by an evil end and depraved desire

choices.english: as to the substance of the work
choices.why: The scholastic distinction between doing what a precept requires and doing it in the manner that orders it to salvation; kept as the technical phrase.
